findings.description: Successful unlocking dispels a fear becomes temporarily pushing thoughts aside.

contexts.japanese:
この部屋に俺を閉じ込めた悪魔が、
もうすぐ出られると思わせて絶望させようと企む罠かもしれないという妄想は、
……今、払われた。

この部屋に俺を閉じ込めた悪魔が、もうすぐ出られると思わせて絶望させようと企む罠かもしれないという妄想は、
......今、払われた。

この部屋に俺を閉じ込めた悪魔が、
もうすぐ出られると思わせて絶望させようと企む罠かもしれないという妄想は、
……今、払われた。
contexts.WH:
I had a vision of the demon who had locked me in this room using this as a trap to give me hope and then make me despair even more,
......but I pushed those thoughts aside for the time being.
contexts.UP:
At that moment, that terrible thought,
that the demon who had locked me in this room might have been using this as a trap to give me hope and then make me despair even more,
......finally stopped haunting me.

findings.sourceReading: The delusion that unlocking might be a trap is now dispelled, immediately after the successful clank and before the visibly dangling unlocked chain.

findings.sourceReading: 悲壮な運命 characterizes their claimed fate as tragic or poignantly desperate. The question asks whether that fate can change with an ordinary charm.

findings.description: MG changes Kanon’s responding to affection into merely receiving it.

contexts.japanese:
なのに、一方的に好意を受け、……自分に出来ることが、それに応えるだけだなんて、
……悲しくて、……そして自分が悔しかった。
contexts.japanesePS3:
なのに、一方的に好意を受け、……自分に出来ることが、それに応えるだけだなんて、
……悲しくて、……そして自分が悔しかった。
contexts.MG:
The fact that he was accepting her affection one-sidedly, unable to do anything but simply receive it,
...made him sad...and frustrated at himself.
contexts.UP:
It made him sad and frustrated that he had always been the one‐sided recipient of her affection...
...and could do nothing but respond to it.

findings.sourceReading: JP distinguishes receiving affection from being able only to respond. OriginalPC75957/75958 and UP retain respond; MG repeats receive and eliminates his responsive action.
findings.alternative: Receive can loosely suggest passive reaction, but the source expressly contrasts receipt with response.

findings.description: UP states Shannon’s rejection of magic without the source’s inferential qualification.

contexts.japanese: 彼女はその時点で、一度は魔法の奇跡と決別したはず。
contexts.japanesePS3: 彼女はその時点で、一度は魔法の奇跡と決別したはず。
contexts.MG: At that point, she supposedly rejected the miracle of magic for a time.
contexts.UP: She put the miracle of magic behind her at that point.

findings.sourceReading: JP 決別したはず gives Ange’s inference. OriginalPC76821/76823 and MG retain supposedly; UP states She put the miracle of magic behind her as an unqualified event.
findings.alternative: The prior account strongly supports the inference, but it does not remove the explicitly inferential wording.
